body.statement:
Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{crit}}\), determine a nonvariational
fixed-\(\alpha\) expression for \(L_n(\kappa_n)\) with a uniform
remainder throughout \(T_n\asymp\log(1/\kappa_n)\), and construct an
honest connected interval attaining that expression.  In particular,
for every \(\lambda\in(0,\infty)\), derive and match the limiting
expected length along sequences satisfying
\(T_n/\log(1/\kappa_n)\to\lambda\).  The result must retain
effect-label testing, agree with the exact \(s=1\) common-outcome
plateau experiment, have a \(\lambda\downarrow0\) converse that
recovers Theorem 2's nonshrinking lower bound, with no matched
below-boundary value claimed without a separate attaining upper bound,
and agree in order with Theorems 1 and 3 as
\(\lambda\uparrow\infty\).  It must strictly extend the known-cutoff
honesty result of Noack and Rothe (2024) by evaluating connected
expected length uniformly over the unknown cutoff \(c_P\).
body.justification: The critical window is the only unresolved region where cutoff entropy and weak-denominator uncertainty remain of the same order, so evaluating it completes the frontier rather than juxtaposing regimes.
body.gap: ArmstrongKolesar2018 evaluates fixed-level length through ordered moduli on convex fixed-index classes; the present experiment is a nonconvex union of translated causal ratio models with an effect-label coordinate.
body.consumer: The resulting formula gives the signal threshold and interval length needed to plan, audit, and interpret fuzzy-RD studies whose operative cutoff is not recorded.

obligation.what_is_open: The fixed-level limiting minimax connected expected length and an attaining honest interval throughout the critical window, including the exact transition point.
obligation.obstruction: The finite mixture proves a nonshrinking converse only below its explicit signal-to-entropy threshold.  Above that threshold its chi-square bound becomes uninformative.  The Lipschitz upper theorem applies only beyond its strong-signal condition, while for \(s>1\) the frozen profile is now disproved at the population level and no replacement upper procedure is available.  At the witness threshold, the first-order coordinate \(\lambda\) alone does not determine the mixture limit because a second-order centering term remains.
obligation.attempted: The translated likelihood mixture was evaluated at \(T_n/\log(1/\kappa_n)\to\lambda\), including the \(s=1\) common-outcome plateau calculation.  Separately, exact projection of the frozen higher-smoothness profile produced a counterexample rather than an upper bound.  These calculations give an explicit one-sided phase constant but neither effect-label testing lower bounds above it nor a matched connected-interval construction.
obligation.partial_result:
The explicit witness already evaluates one side of the critical
experiment.  Put \(C_h=(32/M)^{1/s}\) and
\(C_\psi=256/315\).  Then
\(h_n=C_h\kappa_n^{1/s}\),
\(\log J_n=s^{-1}\log(1/\kappa_n)+O(1)\), and
\[
 nC_\psi\kappa_n^2h_n=C_\psi C_hT_n.
\]
Thus, along \(T_n/\log(1/\kappa_n)\to\lambda\), the displayed mixture
chi-square divergence tends to zero whenever
\(C_\psi C_h\lambda<1/s\).  In that subregion the finite-sample
argument gives
\(\liminf_nL_n(\kappa_n)\ge2a_\star(1-2\alpha)\).  For \(s=1\), the
witness threshold is \(\lambda=315M/8192\).  At equality, the
first-order coordinate \(\lambda\) does not determine this mixture's
limit: the second-order value of
\(C_\psi C_hT_n-s^{-1}\log(1/\kappa_n)\) enters.  Above the witness
threshold its chi-square divergence grows and the construction
supplies no converse.  No honest connected interval with a matched
fixed-\(\alpha\) expected-length constant has been constructed in the
remaining critical region.
